text:
maria: quick design question — proposing a small Priority badge on GPU pool cards to indicate Reserved vs Shared pools, plus an inline min/max stepper next to the pool selector. attaching mock in Figma. wondering about copy & a11y implications.

dan: I like showing priority, helps customers pick without opening the pool modal. two quick asks: 1) can the badge also show a cost hint (tiny) or tooltip? 2) stepper should prevent setting min > max and show guardrail inline.

ash: agree on the guardrail. for copy options: 'Reserved pool' vs 'Dedicated (reserved)' — prefer shorter badge text. tooltip can be "Reserved capacity — guaranteed throughput". cost hint could be a subtle "est. $/hr" in tooltip only.

kevin: implementation notes — adding a tooltip is cheap. stepper behavior: currently our stepper is an input + +/- buttons, but it doesn't announce errors to screen readers. we should convert to a proper number input with aria-invalid and an aria-live region for guardrail messages.

olivia: accessibility checklist: 1) stepper buttons keyboard focusable and labeled with aria-label=\"decrease min instances\", aria-label=\"increase min instances\". 2) when guardrail blocks action, set aria-live=\"polite\" with text like "Minimum cannot exceed maximum". 3) badges should be text+icon not just color to avoid color-only meaning.

sam: from research — customers often confuse "min" meaning min instances vs min GPUs. suggestion: change label to "Min GPUs (instances)" or show a small help link that says "what does Min mean?" which opens a short tooltip with an example. customers also ask for an undo on accidental high min.

maria: good — I'll update mocks: badge text "Reserved" and icon shield, tooltip: "Reserved capacity — guaranteed throughput. Learn more". stepper labeled "Min GPUs" and "Max GPUs". Add tiny secondary line under pool card: "Cost hint available" with link to price breakdown.

dan: UX nit — for compact cards, the extra line may push layout. maybe put cost hint into tooltip on the badge and in the pool detail panel. keep card minimal.

ash: micro-interaction: if user sets min > max we should animate an inline validation message and temporarily highlight the offending value. avoid modal interrupts. :warning:

kevin: backend constraint: we support burst capacity that can exceed max temporarily. UI should distinguish "Max (steady)" vs "Burst cap". otherwise users will think burst is blocked by guardrail. maybe show a small "Burst +" chip.

olivia: wording idea for screen readers: when pool is Reserved, announce "Reserved pool. Guaranteed throughput. Burst allowed up to X GPUs." consider adding aria-describedby linking to burst details.

sam: experiment idea: expose a simple slider for SLO target (latency vs cost) on the same panel — moving slider suggests recommended min/max values and shows estimated spend. could be a later phase but aligns with Optimize.

maria: action items from design review: 1) update Figma with badge + tooltip copy, 2) make stepper a proper number input + aria-live, 3) show "Burst +" chip and separate label for Max (steady), 4) put cost hint only in tooltip/detail panel, 5) include inline guardrail validation (no modal). will ping again when mocks updated.

design-bot: new Figma frame uploaded: "gpu-pool-card/badge-stepper-v2" — <https://www.figma.com/file/x/placeholder> :sparkles:

kevin: thumbs up from eng — I'll follow up with implementation tasks and add a small API flag to indicate burstcap metadata so UI can show numbers.

olivia: I'll draft a short a11y spec for this component and share it in the thread once ready.

maria: thanks all — feel free to drop quick comments on the figma, I'm aiming to ship this as part of the autoscale polish sprint. :rocket:
